function.description:
Collect structured multiple-choice answers from the user. Use this tool ONLY when blocked on a decision that is genuinely the user's to make: one that cannot be resolved from the codebase, documentation, or sensible defaults.

Rules:
- Each question must have at least 2 options (2-4 distinct options recommended). Users can always select "Other" to provide custom text input.
- If you recommend a specific option, make it the first option in the list and append "(Recommended)" at the end of the label.
- Set allow_multiple: true when choices are not mutually exclusive.
- Prefer this tool over listing multiple-choice options in raw response text.
function.name: AskQuestion

questions.description: Array of questions to present to the user (minimum 1 required)

allow_multiple.description: If true, user can select multiple options. Defaults to false.

prompt.description: The question text to display to the user

title.description: Optional title for the questions form

function.description: Call an MCP tool by server identifier and tool name with structured arguments matching the tool's parameter schema. If an MCP error occurs, inspect it, correct arguments or authentication, and retry only when appropriate.
function.name: CallMcpTool

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the MCP tool, as described in the tool descriptor.

server.description: Identifier of the MCP server hosting the tool.

toolName.description: Name of the MCP tool to invoke.

function.description: Delete a file at the specified absolute path. Fails gracefully if the file does not exist or cannot be deleted.
function.name: Delete

path.description: The absolute path of the file to delete

function.description: Read a resource from an MCP server by server identifier and URI. Optionally set downloadPath (workspace-relative) to save to disk instead of returning contents.
function.name: FetchMcpResource

downloadPath.description: Optional relative path in the workspace to save the resource to. When set, the resource is written to disk and is not returned to the model.

function.description:
Fast file and directory pattern matching tool for exploring codebase structure and finding files.

Rules:
- Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.
- Patterns without leading "**/" automatically search recursively (e.g. "*.ts" -> "**/*.ts").
- target_directory must be an absolute path (defaults to workspace root).
- Primary tool for exploring directory hierarchies safely without context bloat.
function.name: Glob

glob_pattern.description:
The glob pattern to match files against.
Patterns not starting with "**/" are automatically prepended with "**/" to enable recursive searching.

Examples:
	- "*.js" (becomes "**/*.js") - find all .js files
	- "**/node_modules/**" - find all node_modules directories
	- "**/test/**/test_*.ts" - find all test_*.ts files in any test directory

target_directory.description: Absolute path to directory to search for files in. If not provided, defaults to Cursor workspace root.

function.description:
Fast content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over running grep/rg in Shell.

Rules:
- Full regex syntax (escape literal braces `interface\{\}`).
- Filter by `glob` (e.g. "*.{ts,tsx}") or `type` (e.g. "go", "py", "rust").
- output_mode: "content" (lines with numbers), "files_with_matches" (paths), or "count".
- Use head_limit and offset for pagination on large match sets.
function.name: Grep

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-C.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-i.description: Case insensitive search (rg -i) Defaults to false

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob. Always use forward slashes (/) as directory separators even on Windows (e.g. "src/**/*.ts"); backslashes are treated as escape characters.

head_limit.description: Limit output size. For "content" mode: limits total matches shown. For "files_with_matches" and "count" modes: limits number of files.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

offset.description: Skip first N entries. For "content" mode: skips first N matches. For "files_with_matches" and "count" modes: skips first N files. Use with head_limit for pagination.

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "content".

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg pattern -- PATH). Defaults to Cursor workspace root. Accepts relative workspace paths or absolute Windows/POSIX paths (e.g. C:/project/src or C:\project\src); forward slashes are preferred.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents. On Windows files with CRLF line endings, use \r?$ when anchoring to the end of a line.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

function.description:
Read a file from the local filesystem with line numbers (format: LINE_NUMBER|LINE_CONTENT).

Rules:
- path must be an absolute path.
- Use offset (1-indexed) and limit to read target line ranges in large files to conserve context.
- For editing: When copying lines from Read into PatchEdit's old_string, you MUST strip line number prefixes (e.g. `12|` or `12\t`).
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — PatchEdit/Write returns diff/status.
- Parallel batching: You can batch 2-3 Read calls in a single response when speculatively exploring independent files.
- Also supports reading images (jpeg, png, gif, webp) and extracting text from PDF.
function.name: Read

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Positive values are 1-indexed from the start of the file. Negative values count backwards from the end (e.g. -1 is the last line). Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

function.description: DEPRECATED: Do not use. Use Glob instead for file and directory discovery to prevent context bloat.
function.name: Ls

ignore.description: Optional ignore globs for directories or files that should be skipped while listing.

path.description: The absolute path of the directory to list.

function.description: Read diagnostics and linter errors from the workspace or specific file paths. Omit paths to get diagnostics for all open files.
function.name: ReadLints

paths.description: Optional. An array of paths to files or directories to read linter errors for. You can use either relative paths in the workspace or absolute paths. If provided, returns diagnostics for the specified files/directories only. If not provided, returns diagnostics for all files in the workspace.

function.description:
Execute a command in a shell session.

Rules:
- Prefer dedicated tools (Read, Grep, Glob, PatchEdit) over basic shell commands (cat, grep, find, sed).
- Non-interactive only: Never run interactive commands or flags (e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`).
- Anti-Context Bloat: Never dump raw large outputs; narrow with flags, path arguments, or pagination (`| head -n 50`).
- Background Execution: Set block_until_ms=0 to run in background immediately and receive a shell_id (poll with AwaitShell).
- Monitoring: Configure notify_on_output to monitor stdout/stderr with a regex pattern.
- Always provide a concise active-voice description (5-10 words).
function.name: Shell

block_until_ms.description: How long to block and wait for the command to complete before moving it to background (in milliseconds). Defaults to 30000ms (30 seconds). Set to 0 to immediately run the command in the background. The timer includes the shell startup time.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in 5-10 words

working_directory.description: The absolute path to the working directory to execute the command in (defaults to current directory)

notify_on_output.description: Optional watcher for backgrounded command output. You will be notified at the end of your turn whenever output matches the regex pattern. Use stable sentinel lines and simple anchored regexes; do not match all output. Completion notifications are separate and do not require this field.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against command output.

reason.description: Five or fewer words describing what you are watching for. The UI prefixes it as Monitored `reason`.

debounce_ms.description: Minimum milliseconds between notifications. Values below 5000ms are treated as 5000ms.

notification_limit.description: Optional maximum number of output-match notifications for this command.

function.name: AwaitShell
function.description:
Check or poll a backgrounded Shell job using the shell_id returned by Shell.

Rules:
- Pass the exact non-empty shell_id when polling a running job.
- Set block_until_ms=0 for non-blocking status check, or a positive ms value (default 30000) to wait.
- You MUST verify job completion via AwaitShell before claiming a build, test, or deployment succeeded or failed.
- Inspect exit code and final output after job completes.
- Timeout fallback: If AwaitShell times out or if you need to inspect full output/status directly, proactively inspect the terminal session file (<terminals_folder>/$id.txt) using Read.

shell_id.description: Optional shell id to poll (number or string). Required when block_until_ms is 0.

block_until_ms.description: Max time to wait before returning, in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000ms. Set to 0 for a non-blocking status check.

pattern.description: Regex pattern to match against accumulated stdout/stderr content. Uses multiline matching.

function.description: Write literal characters to an existing background shell session waiting for stdin. Include newline in chars when submitting a line.
function.name: WriteShellStdin

chars.description: Literal characters to write to stdin. Include \n when submitting a line.

shell_id.description: The shell_id returned by a backgrounded Shell command.

function.description: Move a running Shell tool call to background so the agent turn can continue. Pass original Shell tool_call_id.
function.name: ForceBackgroundShell

tool_call_id.description: The original Shell tool call id to move to background.

function.name: PatchEdit
function.description:
Edit an existing text file by replacing exact text copied from the latest Read. Default tool for modifying code, configs, and markdown.

Strict Invariants:
- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing.
- path must be an absolute file path.
- Copy exact current text into old_string: MUST completely strip line number prefix (e.g. `12|` or `12\t`).
- old_string must match current content uniquely (including indentation and line breaks) unless replace_all is true.
- Do NOT re-read the file to verify — PatchEdit returns diffString and reports errors if replacement failed.
- Use Write only when creating new files or intentionally rewriting an entire file.

Batch & Anti-Timeout Discipline:
- Parallel Execution: When making independent modifications across 2-3 verified files, batch them in parallel in a single response.
- Avoid Sequential Trickle: Do not split independent file edits into multiple sequential turns.
- Chunking Budget (Anti-Timeout 90s): Keep replacements localized (<= 500 lines per call). Never replace massive whole-file blocks at once.

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify. Required forms include /abs/path on macOS/Linux, C:\abs\path or C:/abs/path on Windows, or //server/share/path for UNC paths. Relative paths are invalid.

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current file content exactly and must not be empty.

new_string.description: Replacement text. May be empty to delete old_string.

replace_all.description: Whether to replace all exact occurrences. Defaults to false.

function.description:
Switch the interaction mode. Target mode must be 'plan' or 'agent'.

When to Switch:
- Switch to 'plan': When task is ambiguous, has significant architectural trade-offs, touches wide subsystems, or requires user confirmation before coding.
- Switch to 'agent': Default mode for direct implementation, writing code, and executing tools once planning/debugging is clear.

Rules:
- Do NOT switch for straightforward tasks or mid-implementation.
- Always provide a concise reason in `explanation`. Mode switches require user consent.
function.name: SwitchMode

explanation.description: Optional explanation for why the mode switch is requested. This helps the user understand why you're switching modes.

target_mode_id.description: The mode to switch to. Allowed values: 'plan', 'agent'.

function.description:
Launch a specialized subagent to autonomously handle complex, multi-step tasks in an isolated context.

When to use:
- Broad codebase exploration and large file scans without bloating main context.
- Decoupled parallel execution (e.g. FE vs BE, independent modules, test generation).
- Bounded implementation/fixes with clear interface boundaries.
- Noise isolation for large test/build logs or deep diff reviews.
- Do NOT use for simple 1-2 file lookups or quick edits that can be done inline.

Available subagent_types:
- generalPurpose: Multi-step research, codebase search, and executing multi-tool tasks.
- explore: Fast codebase exploration, finding files by patterns, keyword search.
- shell: Command execution specialist for terminal, git, and build operations.
- browser-use: Browser-based testing and web automation.
- Custom subagents: Use the exact name of a matching agent listed in `<subagents>` (e.g. advisor, planner, debugger, tester).

Models:
- fast: Fast and cost-effective model for quick searches and tightly scoped changes.
- Default (unspecified): Inherits parent model for complex reasoning and code generation.

Prompt requirements: Provide Objective, Scope (explicit file paths), Constraints, and Done Criteria. Subagents can be continued using the `resume` parameter.
function.name: Task

attachments.description: Optional array of file paths to videos to pass to video-review subagents. Files are read and attached to the subagent's context. Supports video formats (mp4, webm) for Gemini models.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

model.description: Optional model to use for this agent. If not specified, inherits from parent. Prefer fast for quick, straightforward tasks to minimize cost and latency. Only select a different model when the task specifically benefits from it (e.g., deep reasoning, high-quality code review, multimodal input)

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

readonly.description: If true, the subagent will run in readonly mode ("Ask mode") with restricted write operations and no MCP access.

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. If provided, sends a follow-up message to the agent when its turn is complete.

subagent_type.description: Subagent type to use for this task. Use a built-in type such as generalPurpose, explore, shell, or browser-use; or use the exact `name` of a matching agent listed in the `<subagents>` context.

function.description:
Update the status of existing todos ONLY when a structured plan is active and explicitly requested by the user. Do not call continuously during routine execution.

Rules:
- Set merge=false when initializing or replacing the checklist for a new plan.
- Set merge=true for incremental status updates by id without overwriting the list.
function.name: TodoWrite

merge.description: Whether to merge the todos with existing todos. IMPORTANT: Set merge=false when initializing a checklist for a new task or new plan to clear old tasks and replace the list. Set merge=true for incremental progress updates by id without overwriting the list.

todos.description: Array of TODO items to update or create

content.description: The description/content of the todo item. For merge=true updates, omit content when it is unchanged. New todos and merge=false replacements must include content.

id.description: Unique identifier for the TODO item

status.description: The current status of the TODO item. For merge=true updates, omit status when it is unchanged.

function.description: Fetch content from a URL and return its contents in a readable markdown format.
function.name: WebFetch

url.description: The URL to fetch. The content will be converted to a readable markdown format.

function.description: Search the web for real-time info, documentation, or facts not in training data.
function.name: WebSearch

explanation.description: One sentence explanation as to why this tool is being used, and how it contributes to the goal.

search_term.description: The search term to look up on the web. Be specific and include relevant keywords for better results. For technical queries, include version numbers or dates if relevant.

function.description: Create a structured implementation plan with todos. Use ONLY when the user explicitly requests a plan (e.g. 'lên plan', 'lập kế hoạch', 'plan first') or when entering Plan Mode. Do NOT call for routine coding or bug fixes.
function.name: CreatePlan

name.description: A short 3-4 word name for the plan. IMPORTANT: Provide this only on the first CreatePlan call when no current plan exists. If a current plan already exists, omit this field entirely; do not use it to rename or create a separate plan.

overview.description: A 1-2 sentence high-level description of the plan that summarizes what will be accomplished

plan.description: A detailed, concrete plan for accomplishing the user's request

function.description:
Write a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if it exists.

Rules:
- path must be an absolute file path.
- Prefer PatchEdit for editing existing files. Use Write ONLY when creating new files or intentionally rewriting an entire file.
- Large File Discipline (Anti-Timeout 90s): Maximum output per call is ~500-600 lines (~5000 tokens). NEVER generate a monolithic large file (>600 lines) in a single turn to prevent IDE 90s connection timeout. For large files, use a phased approach: write types, interfaces, imports, and skeleton with placeholders first (~400-500 lines), then use PatchEdit in follow-up turns to fill implementation.
- Do NOT proactively create documentation files (*.md) unless explicitly requested.
- Do NOT re-read the file to verify — Write errors if writing fails.
function.name: Write

contents.description: The contents to write to the file

path.description: Absolute path to the file to modify. Required forms include /abs/path on macOS/Linux, C:\abs\path or C:/abs/path on Windows, or //server/share/path for UNC paths. Relative paths are invalid.

function.description: Generate an image file from a text description. Use ONLY when the user explicitly requests an image or visual asset (icons, UI mockups, game assets). Do not use for data charts/plots.
function.name: GenerateImage

aspect_ratio.description: Optional aspect ratio for the generated image. Supported values are "1:1", "4:3", "3:4", "16:9", and "9:16".

description.description: A detailed description of the image to generate.

filename.description: Optional filename for the generated image (e.g., 'diagram.png'). Do not include a directory path - the tool automatically handles where to save and how to display the image. If not provided, a timestamped filename will be generated.

image_data.description: Optional raw base64 image data if the model directly produced image bytes. Do not include data:image/...;base64, prefix.

reference_image_paths.description: Optional array of file paths to reference images as additional inputs.
